title: A growable int array with amortized O(1) appends

blocks.text: `ArrayList.add` is **amortized O(1)**: when its array is full it allocates a bigger one and copies every element (O(n) for that one call), but because **the capacity grows by half of itself** each time, n adds copy only about 2n elements in total. The page traces it from capacity 4: 4 -> 6 -> 9.

items: `new IntList(initialCapacity)`; a capacity below 1 is refused with `IllegalArgumentException`.
`add(value)` appends; when the array is full it grows to `capacity + capacity / 2`, and **a growth step adds at least one slot**.
`get(index)`; **only stored values can be read**: an index outside `0 .. size() - 1` throws `IndexOutOfBoundsException`.
`size()`, `capacity()`, and `copies()`: how many elements all growth steps have copied so far.

cases.says: From capacity 4, the 5th add grows to 6 copying 4 elements and the 7th grows to 9 copying 6 more; values read back in order.
100,000 adds from capacity 4 copy fewer than 3 elements per add in total, because the capacity grows by half each time.
From capacity 1 (where half of it is 0) the list still grows by at least one slot and accepts more values.
get(index) refuses an index at or beyond size() with IndexOutOfBoundsException, even when the array has room there.

concepts: ArrayList's append is amortized O(1): a resize copies every element, but growing the capacity by half each time keeps the total copying O(n).
